description:
Spin the base game until a round PAYS, then settle. Mechanism-agnostic: it asks only `payout > 0`, so it works on a payline game as readily as a cascade one — use it for the balance-credit check. (`base-cluster-win` is the cascade-specific cousin: it additionally requires >= 2 cascade steps, which a payline game never produces.) Exposes res = the winning round + facts.spins_to_win / win_payout / win_stake. Unreached if nothing pays inside the spin budget.
It also publishes the BALANCE READOUT'S THREE VALUES for the winning round — balance_before_spin, balance_while_spinning (the stake is taken at spin START, so the readout sits here for the whole spin) and balance_after_win. A prompt about either half of the money has to name the two endpoints of the step it is judging, not just the destination; naming only `res.balance` earned a correct NO on Mah_008, because that is a value the readout passes THROUGH. The names are `base-cluster-win`'s and the authoring doc's, deliberately: one concept must not have two names across two scenarios, or a prompt moved between them silently binds to null. See docs/scenario-assert-authoring.md §2. PORTABLE, and verified against the captured payloads of all three games. The one thing to know is WHY `win_stake` is always > 0 here: a paying round with stake 0 exists on every game with a bonus -- Zeus's terminal Hold & Spin round reports payout 261 at stake 0 and is NOT a trigger, so it reads exactly like a base win. It never reaches this loop because `base_spin()` only returns rounds the framework CLICKED; bonus rounds arrive through `awaitFreespinRound` inside `play_out_freespins`. That is an invariant of the drive, not an accident -- a scenario that collects rounds some other way must re-check it.

cases.title: Placing a bet takes the stake out of the balance

video.prompt:
Grandma Pets is a 5-reel, 4-row slot. This clip is one paid spin — watch the balance and any win amount shown.
(1) balance_drops_on_spin: when the spin starts, does the balance go DOWN? (2) win_amount_shown: is the win amount displayed anywhere when the spin resolves? (3) win_amount_text: read that win amount exactly as printed, as a string. If you cannot read it clearly, answer "unreadable". (4) balance_counts_up: does the balance then increase to its final value? (5) final_balance_text: read the balance at the END of the clip, as a string. (6) ui_broken: is anything overlapping, cut off, placeholder or visibly broken?
notes: one short sentence on anything the questions above do not cover.

data.reason: The balance drops from 15,142.83 to 15,135.83 at the beginning of the spin (00:04). A win of 5.60 is clearly displayed at the end of the spin (00:14) and the balance increments to 15,141.43 (00:17).
